questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: Speaking and Moving in the First Part of the Night
questions.learningObjective: Identify the sleep stage most linked to sleepwalking
questions.stem: Astronomer Rhea notes she walked to the telescope and spoke clearly while still asleep early in the night.

options.text: Sleepwalking and sleeptalking arise mainly in deep NREM sleep early in the night.
They arise mainly in REM sleep, when dreams are vivid and movement is possible.
options.misconception: attributes the events to REM dream sleep

options.text: They arise only after a full night without sleep and extreme fatigue.
options.misconception: ties the events to sleep deprivation alone

options.text: They are purely voluntary movements that occur during very light sleep.

questions.explanation: Sleepwalking and sleeptalking occur mostly in slow-wave NREM sleep in the first half of the night, not during REM. REM atonia normally prevents dream enactment, so attributing them to REM is wrong.
questions.hint: Think about which half of the night deep sleep dominates.

questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: Irresistible Sleep and Sudden Loss of Tone
questions.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism behind narcolepsy with cataplexy
questions.stem: Astronomer Soren describes sudden sleep attacks and knee-buckling laughter; explain the underlying mechanism.

answer.exemplar: Narcolepsy with cataplexy involves loss of orexin neurons, causing sudden sleep attacks and emotion-triggered muscle atonia; the brain cannot maintain stable wakefulness.

questions.explanation: The symptoms point to orexin deficiency disrupting arousal and REM-atonia control. Strong emotion triggers cataplexy because the atonia circuit misfires during wakefulness.
questions.hint: Link the emotion-triggered collapse to REM atonia.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the reduction factor of orexin level
questions.stem: A cerebrospinal fluid sample shows orexin at 40 pg/mL; the normal reference is 200 pg/mL. By what factor is the level reduced?
questions.explanation: Divide the normal reference by the measured level: 200 / 40 = 5. A fivefold reduction matches the orexin loss seen in narcolepsy with cataplexy.
questions.hint: Divide the normal value by the measured value.

Restless legs syndrome, because the legs move at night.

questions.explanation: Snoring plus witnessed apneas plus daytime sleepiness is the classic triad for obstructive sleep apnea. Insomnia, narcolepsy, and restless legs lack the breathing-pause element.

options.text: Hypopnea, from shallow breathing with normal effort.
options.misconception: confuses reduced flow with absent effort

questions.explanation: Central apnea means no breathing effort despite an open airway, reflecting failed respiratory drive. Obstructive apnea shows effort against a closed airway.
